transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sara Lin (Redwood AE), Mark Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kumar (Novapay Head of Platform), Alan Soto (Novapay SRE), Marta Reyes (Novapay PM), Diego Morales (Novapay Eng)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focused on latency tuning. Reviewed TTFT numbers from last run, discussed enabling streaming to reduce perceived latency, looked at sequence length distribution to tune batching, and agreed on kernel A/B tests on staging. Next steps and owners captured at end.

[00:00] Sara: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we are on the weekly sync for the latency tune POC with Novapay, we have mark from engineering, jordan briefly, and lina will drop in later. Priya do you want to kick off with any updates from your side?

[00:12] Priya: yeah thanks Sara. quick update - we ran the ingest for last week's traffic sample, the overall p50 looks fine but p95 and p99 still spiky, we saw some 420-520 ms spikes on certain payloads, we suspect it's long tail sequences and some cold KV cache hits.

[00:28] Mark: okay, that jives with what we saw. the TTFT - time to first token - on the last run was about 80ms median but 230ms p95, streaming off. When we enabled streaming in a quick experiment it dropped first byte to ~40ms median and 150ms p95 so there is a clear user-perceived improvement. there might be tradeoffs on throughput though.

[00:52] Alan: quick q - when you say streaming did you chunk the request on the client or was it server-side chunked responses? we have some concerns about our websocket proxies and connection timeouts.

[01:02] Mark: good question. this was server-side streaming from our runtime using chunked responses. client consumed via SSE in the test harness. Alan, if your proxies close idle connections we can add keepalive or switch to short-lived chunks, it's configurable.

[01:18] Marta: also, about sequence lengths - Diego and I noticed many of our requests are short (<= 128 tokens) but about 7% are long tails up to 1024 tokens. that's where p99 shoots up.

[01:32] Sara: that's super useful, thanks. So two parallel levers: enable streaming for TTFT improvement and optimize kernel selection / batching for long sequence tail. Mark, can you summarize kernel choices? we had conversation last week around fused kernels vs attention-optimized kernels.

[01:48] Mark: sure. on Ampere-like GPUs we tested two kernel sets: kernel set A uses fused attention kernels and is optimized for shorter sequences - it gives better TTFT and p50 but degrades when sequence >512. kernel set B uses attention-slicing kernels which are more stable for long sequences and give better p95/p99 at high seq lengths but slightly worse p50. also quantization (int8) helps throughput but sometimes increases first-token decoding overhead because of extra dequant/decode steps.

[02:14] Priya: hmm, so is there a recommended default for us? most of our traffic is short, but we can't ignore the long tail.

[02:20] Mark: recommendation is dynamic routing or fallback: primary kernel A for short sequences, if seq length over threshold (say 512) route to kernel B or a larger bucket on dedicated instances. that's what Redwood's routing policy can do - automatic fallback or route-by-policy.

[02:37] Priya: is that supported on Dedicated? we are looking at dedicated capacity with some burst to hosted for overflow.

[02:44] Sara: yes, Dedicated supports per-pool kernel config and routing rules; you can set policy to prefer dedicated then host fallback, or vice versa. also you can pin a model variant per pool. we'll share a sample routing config.

[02:59] Alan: security check - if we route to hosted fallback does any PII leave our VPC? our compliance team flagged that.

[03:07] Sara: important point. data routing depends on deployment: if Dedicated is within your VPC, traffic stays inside. hosted fallback would traverse Redwood's network unless you use private deployment. we can do encryption in transit, and KMS for payload keys, but for strict data residency you'd want Private deployment or dedicated within your cloud account. we'll include that in the security doc.

[03:28] Marta: back to TTFT: is the biggest lift enabling streaming on the client or do you have server default switch?

[03:35] Mark: server-side flip is quick - there are two things: enable streaming responses (server config) and enable chunked client consumption to reduce perceived latency. we can push a feature flag on staging and you can test with your existing proxies. the main caveat is ordering and partial responses if you rely on full output to post-process.

[03:52] Diego: for our flow we show incremental suggestions so streaming is actually preferred, it will feel faster to users.

[03:58] Priya: great. about batching: we noticed batching at 8 requests gives good throughput but adds ~60ms to TTFT for short sequences. is there automatic adaptive batching?

[04:09] Mark: yes, our runtime has continuous batching and it can be tuned - target batch size, max delay, and prioritization for low-latency routes. for short-seq critical paths we recommend smaller max-delay (e.g., 5-8ms) and small target batch. we also have prefix KV cache to avoid re-encoding long context.

[04:30] Priya: can you quantify what changing max-delay from 15ms to 5ms does to throughput?

[04:35] Mark: ballpark: reduces effective throughput by ~10-15% but drops TTFT by about 30-40% on short interactions. exact numbers depend on request distribution. we'll run the A/B and share.

[04:48] Alan: any gotchas with quantization for us? our inference once in prod should keep hallucination risk low, do quantization impact quality?

[04:55] Mark: quantization can slightly degrade generation quality on some models, more so at aggressive quant levels. we recommend running evals on your prompt set; Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles per workload. For this POC we tried int8 and q4_0, q5_0 variants; q5 gave the best balance for your use case.

[05:14] Priya: quick note - our compliance team will require SOC2 + audit logs, SSO (SAML), and KMS integration. do you have reference docs?

[05:21] Sara: yes - we'll share the security pack (SOC2 cert, architecture for KMS, SAML SSO guide). I'll attach links in the follow-up.

[05:29] Mark: jumping back to kernels - I propose we run a kernel A/B on staging for a 12-hour window using your 1-hour sample replay. measure TTFT, p50, p95, p99, and token throughput. we'll also test streaming enabled vs disabled.

[05:43] Priya: sounds good. for the A/B do you need us to change anything in our client?

[05:48] Mark: no, we'll run it at the runtime and route variants; you just need to allow the staging endpoints and confirm the sample playback works.

[05:58] Marta: another operational note - if we enable streaming and the client reconnects mid-response, do you support resume?

[06:05] Mark: not resume per se, but the client can detect partial output and request completion. there's an idempotent continuation token pattern we can implement; it's extra work but doable.

[06:15] Sara: let's capture concrete owners and dates - Mark will run kernel A/B and streaming experiment by Friday (2026-08-07). Sara will send pricing and security pack by Thursday (2026-08-06). Priya will upload sequence distribution and sample. Alan will validate proxy keepalive settings. schedule benchmark for 2026-08-11.

[06:34] Priya: ok agreed. any blockers from your side Mark?

[06:37] Mark: none. I'll also include a note on recommended threshold routing (512 tokens) and the config snippet.

[06:44] Diego: small nit - could you include the expected cost delta for dedicated pool vs hosted per 1000 tokens? that'll help our finance team.

[06:51] Sara: yes I'll include cost estimates for typical and heavy tails.

[06:55] Jordan (observer): one more thing - if you plan to use KV cache aggressively, ensure your client sets stable conversation IDs so we can reuse prefixes.

[07:05] Alan: noted.

[07:08] Closing: recap of next steps and owners. Thanks all, we'll reconvene next week at the same time unless we need an earlier benchmark.

Reference artifacts mentioned: "latency-benchmarking-2026-07-31.xlsx" (shared drive), "redwood-routing-sample.yml" (link), security pack (SOC2 + SAML guide) - links to be shared in follow-up.
